liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Me And My Uncle** (1 other source): Announcers are audible when it cuts in; after they stop, recording quality changes, suggesting a radio broadcast or a patched section [1]
- **Alligator** (1 other source): The recording of Alligator starts abruptly, already in the vocals [1]

## The recordings

- **gd69-05-29.sbd.jim.14018.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 14 songs; 73 min; rated 2.1/5 by 10 [1]. Said about its sound: Tape degradation is present at the start of Morning Dew and lessens as the track goes on; Sounds rough for the stated lineage, with at least two cassette generations seemingly involved; Sound quality is poor [1][2][3]

## Around the show

- A late-August 1969 Rolling Stone article covers this show; Garcia was disgusted with the sound system [5]
- The band used the local PA because Bear was absent owing to legal trouble [5]
- Rolling Stone placed Garcia backstage, a curtained-off quarter of the gym, playing his red Gibson with a Red, White and Blue Power sticker [6]
- The performance is chaotic at times, with extra musicians joining in and someone adjusting vocals [10]
- Pig is heard in Bobby's backing vocal slot [10]
- Recommends the Pow Wow shows for cleaner-sounding May 1969 recordings [2]
- Material duplicates what is listed for 5/11/69 San Diego, so the correct date is uncertain [4]
- The reviewer argues the article shows this recording's material comes from some other show [6]
- Considered the best available recording so far, compared with SHNid 6296 [8]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-05-29.sbd.jim.14018.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Steve and; source: Soundboard [1]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Robertson Gym U.C.S.B., Santa Barbara Poster](https://www.dead.net/archives/1969/artwork/robertson-gym-u-c-s-b-santa-barbara-poster) [13]
